parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
Consider the following two equilibria and associated data values at $298\text{ K}$.

$$\text{AgBr(s)} \rightleftharpoons \text{Ag}^+\text{(aq)} + \text{Br}^-\text{(aq)} \text{          equilibrium 1          } K_{\text{sp}} = 5.0 \times 10^{-13}\text{mol}^2\text{dm}^{-6}$$

$$\text{Ag}^+\text{(aq)} + 2\text{NH}_3\text{(aq)} \rightleftharpoons \text{[Ag(NH}_3\text{)}_2\text{]}^+\text{(aq)} \text{          equilibrium 2          } K_{\text{stab}} = 1.7 \times 10^7\text{mol}^{-2}\text{dm}^6$$

The equilibrium constant for equilibrium **1** is the solubility product, $K_{\text{sp}}$, of $\text{AgBr(s)}$. The equilibrium constant for equilibrium **2** is the stability constant, $K_{\text{stab}}$, for the formation of $\text{[Ag(NH}_3\text{)}_2\text{]}^+\text{(aq)}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the solubility of $\text{AgBr}$ at $298\text{ K}$ in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Use Le Chatelier's principle as applied to equilibria **1** and **2** to suggest why $\text{AgBr(s)}$ dissolves in concentrated $\text{NH}_3\text{(aq)}$.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Use equilibria **1** and **2** to construct an equation for the reaction of $\text{AgBr(s)}$ with concentrated $\text{NH}_3\text{(aq)}$. This is equilibrium **3**.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Write an expression for the equilibrium constant of equilibrium **3**, $K_{\text{eq3}}$, in terms of $K_{\text{sp}}$ for equilibrium **1** and $K_{\text{stab}}$ for equilibrium **2**.
